source_title: The Vision of Escaflowne (1996 television anime)
continuity_scope: The original Sunrise television anime, The Vision of Escaflowne / Tenkū no Escaflowne, begun 2 April 1996 and consisting of 26 episodes. Official Sunrise work metadata and an official Crunchyroll series listing are the selected witnesses. No official episode synopsis/profile page with claim-level detail was surfaced, so this is a narrow official-metadata pass. Manga versions, the 2000 film, games, novels, guidebooks, later home-video releases/localizations, and all other adaptations are separate continuities or witnesses.
work_or_witnesses: Sunrise, THE VISION OF ESCAFLOWNE, original 1996 television anime, official work listing
Crunchyroll, The Vision of Escaflowne official series listing
coverage_rule: All named individual dramatic figures in the selected official synopses: Hitomi and Van. Allen is named only in an official Japanese cast list without claim-level role evidence in the selected English synopsis window, so is omitted rather than visually or conventionally inferred. Peoples/species, roles, factions, Guymelefs/mecha, magic/divination, items, Gaea/places, isekai systems, and themes are dimensions or terms rather than nodes.
omissions: Every named or unnamed figure beyond Hitomi and Van in the selected synopsis window, including Allen and all cast not backed by claim-level official synopsis evidence.

All episode-specific developments, named factions, Guymelef mechanics, romance outcomes, magical/divinatory rules, war resolutions, deaths, locations, and later continuity material; all manga, film, games, novels, guidebooks, home-video releases/localizations, and adaptations.
Fan wikis, Wikipedia, databases, reviews, social summaries, and long episode/scene reproduction.
uncertainties: Sunrise provides production date and episode count but no episode-level summaries on the selected work page. This two-character result is complete only under the selected named-synopsis rule.

The selected official English Sunrise page identifies Hitomi's special abilities but does not call them divination or specify their mechanics. Crunchyroll describes Van as newly ordained king and links him to Escaflowne, but does not supply a full mecha/Guymelef system; no more specific terms are inferred.

English localization credits and version differences are not stated in the consulted Sunrise page. Crunchyroll is recorded as a separate official distributor witness, not as evidence that its streaming/localized version is identical to every prior release. The source includes war, violence, world-endangerment, and romance themes; these are fictional content cautions.
evidence_basis: Official Sunrise work metadata and official Crunchyroll series metadata only. No fan or secondary source is used as canonical evidence.
